elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either Party, including the Company as Customer, to terminate the Agreement, and subsection (a) expressly characterizes the Company's termination under Section 4.1 as termination for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Company must provide 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no obligation for HDI to refund prepaid fees pro rata.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either Party, including HDI, to terminate on 90 days' notice and does not expressly limit HDI's termination right to the end of a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Company may terminate for convenience under Section 4.1 on 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is capped at the aggregate amounts payable under Section 3.1 for the three calendar months preceding termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: HDI may terminate on 90 days' notice, but the operative language does not require its termination to occur only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The right granted to either Party requires 90 days' written notice.
